provenance.canonical_layout: The canonical market inputs every reconstruction of this issuer reads: the daily price series and the filing acceptance evidence. They live here, rather than in a historical P/E dataset, because no P/E distribution has been established for this issuer; the income-statement and enterprise-value datasets read both by path, so one trading calendar and one acceptance index serve every reconstruction of it.

daily_prices.json.definition: The daily price series, as traded. American Electric Power has had no stock split in the covered period, so the series needs no split adjustment and the close pairs with the cover-page share count as it stands.

filing_acceptance_evidence.json.source: SEC EDGAR SGML header ACCEPTANCE-DATETIME, one header per filing, from the submissions recent list and the additional submissions files for older filings
filing_acceptance_evidence.json.definition: Each filing's acceptance datetime, read from the filing's own SGML header, with the header's URL and SHA-256 recorded so the timestamp is traceable to the bytes it came from. A fact whose filing is not in this index has no knowability evidence in these datasets and is skipped.

known_limitations: The index covers the filings accepted between 2019-01-24 and 2026-07-30, drawn from the submissions' recent list and from the additional submissions files for the older filings. Filings outside that window are not in the index, so the trailing windows cannot reach further back.

The index holds the periodic filings and the Item 2.02 earnings releases. The earnings releases are furnished evidence, the periodic filings are filed evidence, and the datasets use both under the same acceptance rule.
